fillers: Nobody said a word, but everybody thought the same thing.
That was when the kettle started whistling in Morse code.
Somehow, the dog seemed to understand everything.
The lights flickered, and the room smelled faintly of popcorn.
Nobody wrote that part down, for obvious reasons.
It was, in hindsight, exactly the wrong moment to sneeze.
The crowd gasped, then immediately pretended they had not.
Somewhere far away, a bell rang twice.
And that is how the rumour started.
For a long moment, even the crickets went silent.
Nobody ever found out who moved the ladder.
The plan, such as it was, began to fall apart beautifully.
seeds: The morning the gravity switched off for exactly eleven seconds, Meera was carrying a wedding cake.
Nobody believed the old lighthouse keeper until the whales started spelling words.
My grandmother's recipe book had one page that was definitely not about cooking.
The lost-and-found box at the space station held something that hummed.
On the first day of school, the new kid arrived by parachute.
The town's statue winked at midnight, and only the night baker saw it.
Somewhere under the city, the pigeons were holding elections.
The last library on Earth lent out one book that was never returned, until today.
Aarav woke up to find his shadow filing an official complaint.
The village well granted wishes, but only extremely literal ones.
Every radio in the country played the same unknown song at dawn.
The museum's dinosaur skeleton moved one inch to the left overnight.
I found a door in my apartment that I had never noticed before.
The world's quietest town woke up to a marching band nobody had hired.
Captain Rao's last message from the submarine was just a recipe for soup.
The school hamster escaped, and somehow the traffic lights changed forever.
A package arrived with no address, ticking softly, smelling of mangoes.
The new neighbour watered their garden at 3 AM and the flowers glowed.
Deep in the forest, the trees had started leaving voicemails.
The elevator in our building had one extra button with no number.
On her hundredth birthday, the queen of the ants declared war on picnics.
The lost sock drawer finally opened, and it was a portal all along.
